domain: Information Standards / Sociotechnical Systems / Representational Conventions
topic_summary: Analysis of the ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD) versus US month/day/year (MM/DD/YYYY) date format dispute. The topic presents as a representational standard conflict but examination reveals it is NOT a contested kernel — both formats encode identical information with identical precision, differing only in serialization order. The disagreement is about coordination costs and legacy path dependency, not about what constitutes a valid date representation.

key_entities: ISO 8601 standard (international date/time representation standard, YYYY-MM-DD)
US date convention (MM/DD/YYYY format, dominant in American contexts)
Legacy systems (databases, forms, software expecting specific format)
key_tensions: Lexicographic sortability vs cultural familiarity (ISO advocates vs US convention defenders)
Global interoperability vs domestic coordination equilibrium (international vs national optimization)

omegas.description: Topic flagged as contested kernel but examination reveals collapse: all candidate 'readings' encode identical information (year/month/day) with identical precision. Disagreement is about serialization order (coordination problem) not about what constitutes a valid date (ontological disagreement). The kernel collapses to a single constraint observed from different coordination positions. Decomposed as ordinary axes instead.

Analysis focuses on ISO vs US formats but excludes DD/MM/YYYY (European convention), which creates a three-way coordination problem with different ambiguity patterns. The mountain of lexicographic sortability applies identically; the piton of cultural familiarity has a different geographic distribution. Deferred for scope management.

Is regulatory_mandate_potential a Scaffold (enabling coordination) or a Snare (imposing costs on non-compliant actors)? Depends on whether mandate includes transition support or simply penalizes legacy format use. Deferred axis with high policy sensitivity.

omegas.description: Analysis assumes Gregorian calendar. Non-Gregorian calendar systems (Hebrew, Islamic, Chinese) have fundamentally different date representation requirements. ISO 8601 is Gregorian-only; treating it as universal standard erases non-Western temporal systems. Potential Snare for cultural minorities.
